sentences.text: The genus name means "opposite bird" because it possesses a reversed scapula-coracoid connection compared to modern birds and hesperornithids.
Enantiornis leali is among the largest enantiornithines, reaching about 78.5 cm in length, 34 cm in hip height, 6.75 kg in weight, and a 1.2 m wingspan.
The genus was described based on specimen PVL-4035, which includes a coracoid, proximal scapula, and proximal humerus suspected to be the left shoulder of one individual.
Enantiornis leali belongs to the subclass Enantiornithes.
Enantiornis leali was placed in its own family, Enantiornithidae.
The fossil range of Enantiornis leali is the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian).
The genus Enantiornis lived from the Turonian to the Maastrichtian, between 93.9 and 66 million years ago.
Because no hindlimb elements are known, it is debated whether Enantiornis might include species like Lectavis, Soroavisaurus, or Yungavolucris known only from leg bones.
